summary: A bug in an OpenReview API let anyone reveal the normally anonymous identities of authors, reviewers and area chairs with a simple query. Reports suggest it was exploited from as early as November 11, 2025; ICLR learned of it and alerted OpenReview on November 27, and OpenReview fixed it an hour later. By then author and reviewer data for over 10,000 ICLR 2026 submissions (45% of the conference) had been scraped and circulated online. A commenter posted reviewer identities on 600 papers, and third parties harassed, intimidated and offered bribes to multiple reviewers. ICLR had copies taken down by December 1, reassigned area chairs and reset reviews.
